sentence: The shoulder is built from the clavicle and scapula, which together form the shoulder (pectoral) girdle, and the top of the humerus, which meets the scapula at the shoulder joint.
note: OpenStax 9.6: the glenohumeral joint is the ball-and-socket joint of the shoulder; StatPearls Humerus: the head is the most proximal part and forms the ball of the glenohumeral joint.

sentence: The head of the humerus, the top of the upper arm bone, meets the glenoid cavity of the scapula to form the shoulder joint.
note: StatPearls Humerus: the head forms the glenohumeral joint; OpenStax: head of humerus fits into the glenoid cavity.

sentence: At the top of the humerus the smooth rounded head forms the ball of the shoulder joint.
note: StatPearls Humerus: the head is the most proximal part and forms the ball of the glenohumeral joint.

sentence: The anatomical neck lies just below the head and separates it from the greater and lesser tubercles.
note: Search summary of StatPearls Humerus / Bone Markings: anatomical neck sits below the head, separating it from the tubercles.

sentence: The greater tubercle is on the outer side and the lesser tubercle at the front, and both give attachment to rotator cuff tendons.
note: StatPearls Humerus: greater tubercle lateral, lesser anterior. StatPearls Rotator Cuff: supraspinatus, infraspinatus, teres minor insert on the greater tubercle, subscapularis on the lesser.

sentence: The intertubercular (bicipital) groove runs between the tubercles and holds the tendon of the long head of biceps.
note: Search summary: the intertubercular groove is the furrow between the tubercles and the long head of biceps tendon occupies it.

sentence: Below the tubercles the bone narrows at the surgical neck, where the expanded upper end meets the shaft, and fractures are common there.
note: Search summary: surgical neck is the narrower region below the tubercles where the expanded upper end meets the shaft; fracture lines most commonly appear at the surgical neck.

sentence: The shoulder, or glenohumeral, joint is a ball-and-socket synovial joint in which the rounded head of the humerus fits into the glenoid cavity of the scapula.
note: OpenStax 9.6: the shoulder is a multiaxial ball-and-socket joint; StatPearls: glenohumeral joint is a ball-and-socket synovial joint.

sentence: Ball-and-socket joints have the greatest range of motion of all synovial joints, and OpenStax notes that the shoulder has little in the way of ligament support.
note: OpenStax 9.6: ball-and-socket joints have the greatest range of motion; the shoulder joint has little ligament support.

sentence: This mobility comes at a cost in stability, because the glenoid is a shallow socket and the joint capsule is loose.
note: StatPearls: the capsule is loose, allowing high mobility; the glenohumeral joint is a shallow ball-and-socket. 'Cost in stability' is the author's linking phrase.

sentence: A rim of fibrocartilage called the glenoid labrum runs around the edge of the socket, deepening it and adding stability.
note: OpenStax 9.6: lip of fibrocartilage, the glenoid labrum, extends around the margin; StatPearls: labrum deepens the socket and adds stability.

sentence: Thickened bands within the capsule form the glenohumeral ligaments, which are the main static stabilisers of the joint.
note: StatPearls: thickened bands form the glenohumeral ligaments; they are the primary static stabilisers.

sentence: Muscles add dynamic stability, mainly the rotator cuff and the long head of biceps, whose tendon arises from the top of the glenoid and its labrum and passes through the joint.
note: StatPearls: dynamic restraints are the rotator cuff and long head of biceps; StatPearls Biceps: long head originates at the supraglenoid tubercle and superior labrum and is extrasynovial within the joint.

sentence: The subacromial bursa lies beneath the acromion and deltoid and above the supraspinatus, which it protects from rubbing against the acromion.
note: StatPearls Subacromial Bursitis/Impingement: bursa bordered above by acromion, coracoid, coracoacromial ligament and proximal deltoid, below by supraspinatus; shields the supraspinatus from attrition against the acromion.

sentence: The rotator cuff tendons and this bursa pass through the space between the head of the humerus and the arch formed by the acromion, coracoid process and coracoacromial ligament.
note: StatPearls Impingement: tendons and bursa are compressed between the humeral head and the structures forming the coracoacromial arch.

sentence: The rotator cuff is made up of four muscles, the supraspinatus, infraspinatus, teres minor and subscapularis, often remembered by the letters SITS.
note: StatPearls Rotator Cuff: four muscles, mnemonic SITS.

sentence: Their tendons blend with the joint capsule to form a cuff around the front, top and back of the joint, leaving the lower part relatively unsupported.
note: StatPearls Rotator Cuff: tendons blend with the capsule to form a musculotendinous cuff around the anterior, superior and posterior aspects, leaving the inferior aspect relatively unsupported.

sentence: Supraspinatus helps to stabilise the joint and to start abduction, lifting the arm out to the side.
note: StatPearls Supraspinatus: stabiliser, abduction of the humerus.

sentence: Infraspinatus and teres minor rotate the arm outwards, while subscapularis rotates it inwards.
note: StatPearls: infraspinatus and teres minor assist external rotation; subscapularis produces internal rotation.

sentence: The suprascapular nerve supplies supraspinatus and infraspinatus, the axillary nerve supplies teres minor, and the upper and lower subscapular nerves supply subscapularis.
note: StatPearls: suprascapular nerve to supraspinatus and infraspinatus; posterior branch of the axillary nerve to teres minor; upper and lower subscapular nerves to subscapularis.

sentence: The deltoid arises from the lateral part of the clavicle, the acromion and the spine of the scapula, and attaches to the deltoid tuberosity of the humerus.
note: StatPearls Deltoid: originates from scapular spine, acromion and lateral third of clavicle; attaches to the deltoid tuberosity.

sentence: It has clavicular, acromial and spinal parts, is supplied by the axillary nerve, and is the principal muscle that abducts the arm.
note: StatPearls Axillary Nerve: deltoid has clavicular, acromial and spinous parts, supplied via the anterior and posterior branches of the axillary nerve; deltoid is the principal abductor. One dissection study reports a lateral pectoral nerve contribution to the clavicular part.

sentence: The deltoid abducts the arm, and OpenStax lists flexion, extension and rotation among its other actions.
note: OpenStax glossary: deltoid abducts the arm and also flexes and medially rotates it, and extends and laterally rotates it.

sentence: The axillary nerve comes from the posterior cord of the brachial plexus and passes through the quadrangular space beside the surgical neck of the humerus, together with the posterior circumflex humeral artery.
note: StatPearls: axillary nerve from the posterior cord; quadrangular space bounded laterally by the surgical neck and contains the axillary nerve and posterior circumflex humeral artery.

sentence: The suprascapular nerve comes from the upper trunk of the brachial plexus and passes through the suprascapular notch.
note: StatPearls Suprascapular Nerve: from the upper trunk; passes through the suprascapular notch.

sentence: The anterior and posterior circumflex humeral arteries arise from the axillary artery and together supply the shoulder joint, while the suprascapular artery supplies supraspinatus and infraspinatus.
note: Search summary of StatPearls: both circumflex humeral arteries arise from the axillary artery and supply the glenohumeral joint; the suprascapular artery supplies supraspinatus and infraspinatus.

sentence: The rotator cuff muscles stabilise the joint as the deltoid, the principal abductor, lifts the arm.
note: StatPearls: rotator cuff muscles initiate abduction and stabilise the glenohumeral joint while the deltoid abducts the arm.

sentence: A dislocated shoulder means the upper arm bone has come out of its socket.
note: NHS: dislocated shoulder is when the upper arm bone comes out of the socket.

sentence: The NHS advises going to A&E if the arm cannot be moved, the shoulder looks out of place or has changed shape, or it is painful, bruised or swollen.
note: NHS Dislocated shoulder: go to A&E if you cannot move your arm, the shoulder looks out of place or changed shape, or it is painful, bruised or swollen.

sentence: Treatment is usually a reduction in hospital, in which a clinician moves the bone back into place, followed by a sling.
note: NHS: a doctor moves the arm back into place, after a local anaesthetic or sedative; a sling is then provided.

sentence: The axillary nerve is the nerve most often injured in shoulder dislocation, causing weak lifting of the arm to the side and loss of feeling over the outer upper arm.
note: StatPearls Axillary Nerve Injury / PMC multicentre study: axillary nerve most commonly affected; loss of abduction and of sensation over the outer upper arm.

sentence: Most such nerve injuries recover, and numbness, pins and needles, or arm movement that does not improve is a reason to contact a GP.
note: PMC study: neurapraxia or axonotmesis predominated; NHS trust advice: contact GP or MSK practitioner if numbness or pins and needles develop or movement does not improve.

sentence: A fracture of the proximal humerus, the top of the upper arm bone, causes pain, swelling and difficulty moving the arm, and bruising can spread to the chest, elbow and forearm.
note: Gateshead NHS leaflet: pain and swelling in the upper arm, difficulty moving, bruising spreading to chest, elbow and forearm.

sentence: Many of these fractures do not need surgery, and a sling is the usual first step.
note: NHS trust leaflets: many do not require surgery; a sling is the usual first step.

sentence: A suspected fracture needs assessment in A&E, and increasing pain, swelling, numbness or pins and needles afterwards needs urgent review.
note: Trust leaflets advise urgent review if pain, swelling, pins and needles or numbness worsen; assessment in A&E is the site's route-to-care wording for a suspected fracture and was not stated in the returned text.

sentence: Rotator cuff problems range from irritation of the tendons, called tendinopathy or tendinitis, to partial or full-thickness tears.
note: Search summary of MedlinePlus and NHS trust leaflet: tendinitis is irritation; a tear is partial or full thickness.

sentence: Tears can develop over time or suddenly, for example after a fall onto an outstretched arm or lifting something heavy.
note: Search summary: tears happen over time or suddenly from an injury such as falling on an outstretched arm or lifting something heavy.

sentence: Larger tears tend to cause more weakness, and night pain is common.
note: Search summary: the larger the tear the more weakness; tears often cause pain at night.

sentence: Most people start with non-surgical care such as physiotherapy, and surgery is considered for some tears.
note: Search summary: most start non-surgical, physical therapy; provider may suggest surgery if the tear is large or recent or symptoms persist.

sentence: Arm weakness straight after a sudden injury needs prompt assessment, through NHS 111 or a same-day GP appointment.
note: MedlinePlus: if the arm feels weak right after a sudden shoulder injury, see a provider as soon as possible. The NHS 111 / same-day GP wording is the site's urgent-care route.

sentence: Shoulder impingement is pain that arises when the rotator cuff tendons and subacromial bursa are compressed beneath the arch above the humeral head, and it typically hurts when the arm is lifted forwards or sideways.
note: StatPearls Impingement: tendons and bursa compressed between the humeral head and the coracoacromial arch; pain on forward elevation and abduction.

sentence: In frozen shoulder the joint capsule tightens and becomes inflamed, causing pain and stiffness, often with night pain.
note: NHS 111 Wales and NHS trust leaflets: capsule tightens and inflames; pain and stiffness; night pain common.

sentence: The cause is often unclear, but it is linked to diabetes, thyroid disorders and previous shoulder injury or surgery.
note: NHS trust leaflets (search summary): cause often unclear; associated with diabetes, thyroid disorders, previous injury or surgery.

sentence: It passes through painful, stiff and recovering stages, and NHS 111 Wales advises seeing a GP if shoulder pain and stiffness do not go away.
note: NHS leaflets: three stages (freezing, frozen, thawing); NHS 111 Wales: see a GP if pain and stiffness do not go away.

sentence: Ball-and-socket joints have the greatest range of motion of all synovial joints (Shoulder joint key fact); the other new key facts restate body sentences ledgered above.
note: As ledger entry for the joint section. 'Common causes of persistent pain' restates the clinical sections; NHS 111 Wales and MedlinePlus treat these as common shoulder problems only implicitly - second pass to check.
